sections.h2: Who keeps property records in Williamson County?
sections.html:
That job belongs to the Williamson County Clerk, whose Official Public Records hold deeds, liens, lien releases, plats, restrictions, trusts and similar instruments. The clerk also staffs the probate court, the commissioners court and local birth, marriage and death registration, but land recording is the part a home seller touches. Each deed, deed of trust release and lien notice tied to a Williamson County house lands in that file.

  • Land recording and vital records counter: 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626.
  • Court filings: the Justice Center, 405 Martin Luther King St., Georgetown.
  • Phone: 512-943-1515. Mail: PO Box 647, Jarrell, TX 76537-0647.
  • Hours: the recording counter runs 8 a.m. to 4:30 on weekdays, and the court floor stays open half an hour longer.

Under Attorney General Opinion WW-607, clerk staff cannot search records on your behalf or offer legal advice. You search online yourself, or a title company does it for you.

Start at the clerk's Search Records page, which offers the Official Public Records Search, a judicial records search and a lookup for military discharge records.

Type the owner name from your deed or tax bill, then read forward from that deed. You are hunting for anything recorded afterward: a deed of trust, a release of lien, an abstract of judgment, a notice of foreclosure sale or an affidavit. The usual reason a lien still shows against a house the owner believes is paid off is a release that never got recorded. Under Local Government Code 192.007, any action on a recorded instrument has to be made by recording another instrument in the same manner, so the lender must file that release in this same office.

A map viewer on the county site helps too. Value and ownership data sit at the Williamson Central Appraisal District, yet its roll can lag behind recorded deeds. To learn who holds title, rely on the clerk.

sections.h2: What a deed needs to be accepted
sections.html:
To be recorded, a deed needs the owner's signature and either an acknowledgment taken by a notary or other authorized officer, or an oath before two witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). Owners who live out of state still record a Georgetown house in Georgetown.

Bring a current photo ID along with the document and payment, a requirement tied to House Bill 1195 of the 88th Legislature.

The clerk accepts many instrument types: general warranty, special warranty, quitclaim, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, plus affidavits, leases, sale contracts and powers of attorney. Filing a flawed deed does not cure it. The record simply tells the public what the paper says.

Williamson County posts its own totals in a 2024 Recording Fees PDF on the Fees page, so confirm the exact figure with the clerk. State law sets this base.

Statutory recording charges for a Texas county clerk
ChargeAmount
First page$5.00
Each added page, part page or attachment$4.00
Each name over five indexed$0.25
Records management and preservationUp to $10
Records archiveUp to $10
Records technology and infrastructure$2.00

Leave the grantee's mailing address off a deed and another $25 may apply. Some commissioners courts waive real property recording fees for buyers in particular grant programs. Ask whether Williamson County does.

sections.h2: Guarding against a fraudulent deed or lien
sections.html:
The clerk offers Property Fraud Alert at no charge. Register a name and you get an email or call each time a new document is filed under it.

When a judgment lien or conveyance on your house looks fake, the District Clerk runs a four-step cleanup.

  • Petition the District Clerk.
  • File an Owner's Affidavit of Purported Conveyance.
  • A district judge reviews the filing and signs findings of fact and conclusions of law.
  • File a certified copy of the signed order with the Official Public Records, free of charge.

The process rests on Government Code 51.902 and 51.903, and the District Clerk can tell you about a temporary restraining order. See a lawyer before filing.

Foreclosure auctions take place on each month's first Tuesday, outside the Justice Center at 405 MLK Street in Georgetown.

Lenders have to give notice of sale at least three weeks ahead, post it at the courthouse door and file it with the clerk. A borrower handed a notice of default has 20 days from receipt to reinstate by paying what is past due.

Any notice recorded against your house is searchable at the clerk. A sale before the auction date is possible, with the lender paid out of the buyer's money. Get the servicer's payoff figure in writing.

sections.h2: Recording transfers after an owner dies
sections.html:
The right document depends on how the estate is settled.

  • Transfer on death deed: record an affidavit of death with the death certificate.
  • Administered estate: record the executor's or administrator's deed.
  • Muniment of title: record the court's order along with the will.
  • No court case: an affidavit of heirship, which is a sworn statement and one a buyer need not accept.

Probate staff in the clerk's office accept applications and small estate affidavits. Chapter 205 of the Estates Code limits those to estates with no will and at most $75,000 in assets beyond homestead and exempt property, and a court must approve.

Nobody at the county can add heirs to an old deed. The person taking title records the proving paper, then the sale deed follows.

Sellers often fear a lien will block the sale. Usually it will not, since paying it off at closing clears it. A title company finds what was recorded, asks for the payoff and arranges the release, and it will chase a lender that never filed one.

  1. Run your own name through the county's public records search.
  2. Write down each deed of trust, judgment or lien that turns up.
  3. Request a payoff statement or release from every holder.
  4. Share the list with your title company before any contract is signed.

With a cash buyer there is no loan underwriting, so closing speed depends mainly on how quickly those releases come in.

Williamson County is home to an estimated 752,827 people, 23.6 percent more than in April 2020. About 66.4 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. Median home value is $447,000 and median gross rent is $1,796. With 4,956 building permits issued in 2025, new construction competes with resale listings.

Fast growth means many houses sit under recent deeds and loans, so their records are quick to review. Rural parcels, inherited homes and any house with an unreleased lien need paperwork cleanup before closing.

faqs.q: Does the Williamson County Clerk run searches for me?
faqs.a: No. Clerk staff do not search records for the public, under Attorney General Opinion WW-607. Use the online Official Public Records Search or ask a title company.

faqs.q: Is photo ID required at the recording counter?
faqs.a: Yes. Bring a current photo ID with the document and payment, a rule tied to House Bill 1195.

faqs.q: Where can I find the exact recording fee?
faqs.a: On the clerk's Fees page, which links the 2024 Recording Fees PDF. The statutory figures in the table above are only the base.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Williamson County house with a lien on it?
faqs.a: Often yes, since a lien can be paid at closing. A title company can find the recorded lien, request the payoff and arrange the release, even when the lender never recorded one.

faqs.q: Is the county clerk the same office as the tax office?
faqs.a: No. The tax assessor-collector and the Williamson Central Appraisal District are separate offices. The clerk records documents and keeps probate and commissioners court records.
